    `app-crap-gate` job merges the lcovs and runs the pinned analyzer —
    widget-test coverage differs from the core's dart lcov, E2).
  - The app ladder (follow-up cards, NOT this one): 2450 → 870 → 702 → 650
    → 380 → 272 → 210 (done: `JsAppEngine._faCall` 2450→6 via map
    dispatch, `patch` 94→19, `_tokenize` 70→18; issue #475:
    `wasm_shell_git.run` route-table + 51 golden tests, app `main()`
    boot-phase helpers, `wasm_shell` beasts `_grepBuiltin` 812→covered
    parse helpers, `_runPipeline` 702→210, `_runStage` 600→380,
    `_parsePrimary` 506→210; issue #558: the wasm_shell pipeline engine
    (`_runStage` 380→4, `_runPipeline` 210→4, `_evalExpr` 182→3); issue
    #559: the wasm_shell builtins (`_xargsBuiltin` 272→7,
    `_TestEvaluator._parsePrimary` 210→3, `_trBuiltin` 210→4,
    `_testBuiltin` 132→9, `_duBuiltin` 132→3, `_expandTrSet` 110→gone,
    `_tacBuiltin` 90→6, `_pipBuiltin` 72→3 — spec/table-driven parse
    helpers in `wasm_shell_builtins.dart` + tested exec halves) → next
    milestone 210-class (`GemmaService.chatStream` — gh-2004 since removed, `_statBuiltin` 156,
    wide_layout 156 pair) → … → **40**, each step "fix the code, then
    lower the threshold" — never lower first.
  - Guards (`scripts/check_crap_guards.py`): README badge == config
    threshold for BOTH packages, generated-exclude parity between the
    two configs, and `--only-down` (a PR that raises any threshold vs
    the merge base is rejected in CI).
- Max 2800 lines per `.dart` file (crap4dart `loc` gate, issue #1234 —
  generated output excluded in the gate configs; `*.g.dart` exempt).
- CI layout: `changes` (path filter) → parallel `static`, `test-core`
  (3 duration-balanced shards, `scripts/test_shards.json`, rebalanced
  weekly from junit durations; shard jobs emit junit-shard-N artifacts and
  `shard_files.py` bin-packs manifest-missing new test dirs at runtime),
  `coverage-gate`, `guards`, `flutter-tests` (ubuntu; goldens stay
  host-locked in build-macos.yml) → one aggregate `Quality gate`
  required check, plus `step-timings` (per-step duration telemetry) and a
  `watchdog` (>2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out PR leg gets ONE
  empty-commit retrigger — never `gh run rerun`, which reallocates into
  the same degraded runner pool). `perf-gate` (issue #303) folds the #262
  DoD `dart test --tags perf` trajectory gate into the aggregate for
  trajectory-touching PRs. Issue #551 adds the `integration-mock` leg to
  the aggregate for `test/integration/**` PRs (no-key legs via
  MockLlmServer); the tag-only `integration` job is just the llm provider
  smoke and `publish` waits on it. Issue #1267 N1 adds the
  `flutter-app-exzone` leg: it runs the macOS exclusion-zone family
  (`flutter_app/test/apps/` — JS-engine tests the ubuntu leg skips via
  `native_test_guard.dart`, plus `flutter_app/lib/apps/` + `lib/src/js_ext/`
  are the code that surfaces there) on macos pre-merge, closing the
  nightly-only gap the #1309 escape rode. Under this repo's dispatch-only
  CI the leg is path-blind: ci.yml has no `pull_request` trigger (SM
  `workflow_dispatch` validation is the PR gate), so the leg runs in every
  SM validation dispatch (gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom); the
  `flutter_app/lib/apps/**`/`lib/src/js_ext/**`/`flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`
  path set in the `changes` job only narrows a future real `pull_request`
  trigger. Tag/schedule/release runs skip it — gh-1538 retired the
  nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg is the macOS
  coverage for the JS-engine surface (with gh-1537 there are no main ci
  runs at all — the SM validation dispatch is the single test gate).
  **Nightly (gh-1538) is builds + integration-only**: `nightly.yml` keeps
  the release-mode build matrix (all store/desktop targets) + PTY/CLI
  integration (full real-provider suite with secrets, un-quarantined per
  gh-1199); unit shards, analyze, coverage, CRAP/jscpd and the duplicated
  cli-visual / flutter-app-macos legs moved out as pre-merge-gate

  coverage weekly and files an ai-teammate "raise coverage to X" issue —

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type must exist on BOTH the CLI
(`lib/src/cli/`) and the Flutter app (`flutter_app/lib/`) unless it is
**fundamentally impossible** on the target platform. When a setting or prompt
type is platform-only (e.g. MCP servers need process spawning — impossible on
web), it MUST be explicitly listed in `cliOnlySettings` or `appOnlySettings`
in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` with a comment explaining WHY.

**Workflow when adding a new setting or interactive type:**
1. Add it to `SharedSetting` enum in `settings_registry.dart` FIRST
2. Implement on BOTH platforms (CLI + Flutter app)
3. If one platform genuinely cannot support it: add to the exemption set
   with a one-line reason comment
4. Run `dart test test/parity/` — the parity guard must pass

**Capability rules (issue #1079, host-wiring SDK layer):** every NEW
host-wiring capability declares its matrix state AT BIRTH — for all seven
hosts (`cli`, `macos`, `ios`, `android`, `web`, `extension`, `outlook`) a
state: `on`, `off(reason)`, or `transport(choice, reason)` for a
partial/different transport. The record types, validation and transport
vocabularies live in `lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`; the
seven built-in profiles — where those per-host cells are actually
declared — live in `lib/src/hosts/host_wiring_builder.dart`. The
matrix-completeness test rejects undeclared capabilities, so "CLI got X,
app didn't" cannot happen silently. A capability that is
`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

import pickle, re
with open('/tmp/sections.pkl','rb') as f:
    sections = pickle.load(f)

def clean(txt):
    # strip timestamps
    return re.sub(r'^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T[\d:.]+Z ', '', txt, flags=re.M)

def show_errs(name, ctx=8):
    print('#'*100)
    print('JOB:', name)
    body = sections.get(name, '')
    if not body:
        print('  (missing)')
        return
    body = clean(body)
    lines = body.splitlines()
    # print error-ish lines with context
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        if '##[error]' in l or 'FAILED' in l or 'Some tests failed' in l or '✖' in l:
            lo = max(0, i-ctx); hi = min(len(lines), i+ctx+1)
            print(f'--- context around line {i} ---')
            print('\n'.join(lines[lo:hi]))
            print()

show_errs('24_Build Android APK (debug).txt')
show_errs('46_Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR).txt')
EOF

content.text:
## 3.7.0

- Update bundled OpenSSL for SQLCipher to 4.0.3.
- Add `RawPreparedStatement.columnBytes` and `RawPreparedStatement.columnBlobInto`, which copies a
  column into an existing buffer instead of allocating a new list for each value.
- Hooks: `defines` accepts a map with per-OS entries and a `default`, like `source` and `name`.
- Add `CommonDatabase.status()` reporting status counters.
- Add `Database.releaseMemory()` on native platforms.

## 3.6.0

- Hooks: Support relative paths in `additional_includes` and `additional_lib_directories`.
- Hooks: Support multiple source files to compile with `source: source`.
- Hooks: `source` and `name` accept a map with per-OS entries and a `default` (e.g. `source: {android: system, default: sqlite3}`). Names containing a path (like `foo.framework/foo`) are passed to the loader as-is with `source: system`.
- Update SQLCipher to version 4.19.0.
- Linux: Pre-compiled libraries now support glibc 2.24.x as a minimum version (was 2.38.x before).
- Fix `IndexedDbFileSystem.flush()` not awaiting an ongoing write transaction.

## 3.5.2

- Fix `WasmSqlite3.loadFromUrl` silently dropping request headers and a custom WASM loader.
- Fix OPFS atomics VFS causing IO errors for files larger than 2GB.
- Upgrade SQLCipher to 4.18.0.

## 3.5.1

- Upgrade SQLite to 3.53.4 and SQLite3 Multiple Ciphers to 2.5.0.

## 3.5.0

- Add `CommonPreparedStatement.raw` and `RawPreparedStatement`, providing raw access to prepared statements. On the web, this also allows binding JS big integers directly.

## 3.4.0

- Add `VirtualFileSystemFileV1`, allowing VFS implementations in Dart to implement `xFileControl` and `xSectorSize`.
- Enable `SQLITE_ENABLE_BATCH_ATOMIC_WRITE` to support atomic writes on compatible VFS implementations.
- IndexedDB fileystem: Add `writeAutomatically` option. When disabled, writes are not automatically
  persisted and one needs to call `flush` manually. This explicit control can make database access more
  efficient in some cases.
- IndexedDB filesystem: Restructure IndexedDB code to use much fewer transactions, improving performance.
- Update SQLite to 3.53.3, SQLite3 Multiple Ciphers to 2.3.6 and SQLCipher to 4.17.0.
- Mark a few functions as `isLeaf`, reducing the native overhead of calling them.
- Reset statements after `execute` and `select`.
- Allow custom download URLs for pre-compiled binaries through the `url_pattern` user-define.

## 3.3.4

- Build hook: Fix assets being re-downloaded too often.

## 3.3.3

- Restore support for SQLCipher (thanks to [@davidmartos96](https://github.com/davidmartos96)!).
- Fix crash when loading IndexedDB databases with blocks past the file length ([#380](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/issues/380)).
- Don't uninstall update hooks when closing databases if no update hooks
  were installed by this package.

## 3.3.2

- Support `package:native_toolchain_c` versions `0.18.x` and `0.19.x`.
- Support `hooks` versions `2.x`.

content.text:
## 3.9.1

- Hook: Improve error message when a download from GitHub releases fails.

## 3.9.0

- Add `CommonDatabase.trace`, reporting statement trace events through a
  callback registered with `sqlite3_trace_v2`.
- Add `Database.interrupt()` and `Database.isInterrupted` on native platforms.
- IndexedDB file system: Treat unexpected abort events as errors.
- Update SQLCipher to version 4.20.0.

## 3.8.0

- Fix `InMemoryFileSystem` (and `IndexedDbFileSystem`, which reads through it)
  copying the rest of the file on every read when compiled with dart2wasm,
  which made opening a database quadratic in its size.
- Add `RawPreparedStatement.busy`.
- Fix a number of memory safety violations, mostly on the web.

## 3.7.1

- Update SQLite to 3.54.0.
- Update SQLite3 Multiple Cipher to 2.6.1.

## 3.7.0

- Update bundled OpenSSL for SQLCipher to 4.0.3.
- Add `RawPreparedStatement.columnBytes` and `RawPreparedStatement.columnBlobInto`, which copies a
  column into an existing buffer instead of allocating a new list for each value.
- Hooks: `defines` accepts a map with per-OS entries and a `default`, like `source` and `name`.
- Add `CommonDatabase.status()` reporting status counters.
- Add `Database.releaseMemory()` on native platforms.

## 3.6.0

- Hooks: Support relative paths in `additional_includes` and `additional_lib_directories`.
- Hooks: Support multiple source files to compile with `source: source`.
- Hooks: `source` and `name` accept a map with per-OS entries and a `default` (e.g. `source: {android: system, default: sqlite3}`). Names containing a path (like `foo.framework/foo`) are passed to the loader as-is with `source: system`.

  # gh-1005: Terminal visual is platform-independent and pinned to hosted
  # linux arm64. Evidence: every assertion reads the xterm terminal BUFFER /
  # screen text (never pixels — each PNG even ships a .txt twin "for
  # pixel-independent verification"), rendering goes through the BUNDLED
  # JetBrainsMono font (no host system fonts), and pty2 allocates the PTY
  # via libc openpty FFI. Nothing needs macOS — the old fa-m5 / macos-latest
  # routing (10x hosted-macOS minute cost, single-runner queue risk) is
  # gone; gh-1538 retired the nightly eyeball-only duplicate, so this PR
  # leg is the only screenshot run.
  pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get
      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks — the cli_visual harness
      # spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` from the repo root and its boot budget
      # must not pay the cold-hook cost (tui_prototype_snapshot ×5).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
        env:
          # Issue #1391: same load-stretch as the PTY/CLI shards above —
          # this merge-blocking leg drives the real CLI through the same
          # harness waits and shares the dispatch-wave packing.
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-screenshots-pr
          path: test/integration/screenshots/
          retention-days: 7

  coverage-gate:
    name: Coverage ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, test-core]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — coverage ratchet green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          # gh-1477: blobless full history — the ratchet reads coverage
          # metadata + base...head commit ranges, never historical blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: coverage-shard-*
          path: coverage-shards

      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o coverage/lcov.info coverage-shards/*/lcov.info

      # PRs pay the ratchet on CHANGED lines only (issue #177 wave 2): the
      # 80% bar applies to the diff; main/tags keep the full-suite ratchet.
      - name: Diff coverage ratchet (PR, changed lines >= 80%)
        if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/diff_coverage.py
          --lcov coverage/lcov.info
          --base ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          --head ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          --min 80

# sharded test legs, each leg no longer waits for it.
  flutter-analyze:
    name: Flutter app analyze (ubuntu)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at pub-get/test-build time, so the
      # placeholders must exist BEFORE flutter pub get. Content mirrors the
      # proven build-macos.yml incantation (bare `touch` produced "No file or
      # variants found for asset: .env" on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4).
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored; the tracked placeholder makes it
      # compile (Firebase init is skipped for YOUR_* values at runtime).
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # gh-1296 NG1: the Podfile.lock half of the lockfile gate. pub get just
      # generated .flutter-plugins-dependencies; the gate fails the PR when a
      # native iOS/macOS plugin resolved by the committed pubspec.lock has no
      # pod in the platform's Podfile.lock, or its pod is pinned at a stale
      # version vs the resolved podspec (the gh-1274 class; the historical
      # flutter_gemma 1.8.0-vs-1.11.3 skew motivated it). Self-tested in
      # Static gates (AC2).
      - name: Lockfile pod-sync gate (gh-1296 NG1)
        run: bash scripts/check_lockfiles.sh pod-sync

      # Issue #1234: the flutter_app ≤2800-line guard moved into the app
      # crap4dart.yaml loc gate — enforced whole-tree by the app-crap-gate
      # job's `crap4dart check --baseline` (app_localizations.dart is
      # gen-l10n output, excluded in the gate config). The shell find-exec
      # guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone.

      - name: flutter analyze
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings

  # flutter_app tests sharded ×2 by a deterministic modulo split of the
  # sorted suite (same file list as before — golden + cli_visual stay out,
  # host-locked): each leg is ~half the test phase; pub-cache shared with
  # flutter-analyze so a warm leg pair reuses downloads.
  flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Bootstrap via git
      # clone instead: flutter_tools pulls the official arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: this leg runs on ubuntu
      # and the baselines are macOS-captured. Goldens are guarded by the
      # pinned-font leg in the nightly build-release macOS row (issue
      # #1856): the test env renders every glyph from bundled fonts, so a
      # golden diff fails the same way on any host (#177 E5/OQ3).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (macOS-captured baselines, see the golden
        # comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      # gh-1724 review follow-up: same gh-1412 one-shot retry as the other
      # sharded evidence legs — app-crap-gate hard-fails its merge on

- name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      - name: Download AAB artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: android-aab
          path: flutter_app/aab/

      - name: Setup Ruby
        # ubuntu-24.04 runner images ship no Ruby — `bundle: command not
        # found` exit 127 (issue #353). Same setup as store-metadata.yml.
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@de492cf36cbab201753d720ce4f4e336cd688c94 # v1.328.0 (branch head; v1 moves)
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2'

      - name: Install fastlane
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: bundle install

      # Mirrors submit-ios: without the Play service account the upload
      # skips neutrally (the AAB stays on the GitHub release / artifacts).
      # Track policy (issue #289): manual dispatches default to the
      # internal track; the daily Play leg passes beta (external/open
      # testing). PLAY_VALIDATE_ONLY=1 flips the lane into a dry run.
      - name: Upload AAB to Google Play
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
          PLAY_TRACK: ${{ inputs.android_track }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Play service account not configured — skipping the Play upload (the AAB stays on the GitHub release / artifacts)."
            exit 0
          fi
          AAB_PATH="$(find "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/flutter_app/aab" -name '*.aab' -type f | head -1)"
          echo "Uploading $AAB_PATH to the Play '$PLAY_TRACK' track..."
          ANDROID_AAB_PATH="$AAB_PATH" bundle exec fastlane android upload_only

      # Issue #947: android_content=all means the LISTING ships too. The
      # listing lane replaces the whole image set per locale + device type
      # (supply appends, which is how a stale rejected screenshot survived
      # on the live listing) and verifies the committed state via
      # edits.images.list. Runs after the AAB upload so a release train
      # never ships a binary against a stale listing.
      - name: Deploy Play listing (metadata + images)
        if: inputs.android_content == 'all'
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
          PLAY_TRACK: ${{ inputs.android_track }}
          PLAY_DEPLOY_METADATA: 'true'
          PLAY_DEPLOY_IMAGES: 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Play service account not configured — skipping the listing deploy."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "Deploying the Play listing (texts + images)..."
          bundle exec fastlane android play_store

  build-android-apks:
    # Issue #622: the flavor matrix. The AAB job above stays the Play
    # pipeline (store, unchanged); this job builds BOTH release APKs from
    # ONE variable — FLAVOR drives both the gradle --flavor and the
    # FA_FLAVOR dart-define (contract: the pair must never drift). god
    # (applicationId dev.fa1.app.god) is sideload-only and NEVER reaches
    # Play (binding threat model): it ships as an APK attached to the
    # GitHub release. store keeps its AAB for Play and additionally gets
    # an APK for direct installs + the UT-CI-1 size-delta tracking.
    name: Build Android APK (${{ matrix.flavor }})
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        flavor: [store, god]
    env:
      FLAVOR: ${{ matrix.flavor }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # Same placeholder-.env incantation as build-android (issue #368):
      # .env is a declared Flutter asset and newer flutter validates
      # assets at build time.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors build-android, gated to the store flavor: the secret file
      # carries ONLY the dev.fa1.app client, while the god applicationId is
      # dev.fa1.app.god — overwriting it would hard-fail the google-services
      # plugin ("No matching client found for package name
      # 'dev.fa1.app.god'"). god builds with the committed placeholder
      # google-services.json, which carries both clients.
      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ "$FLAVOR" != "store" ]; then
            echo "$FLAVOR builds with the committed placeholder google-services.json — the secret file has no dev.fa1.app.god client"
          elif [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written"
          else
            echo "GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 not set — building with the committed placeholder google-services.json"
          fi

      # gh-1655: same NDK pre-install as ci.yml build-android — the
      # flavor matrix's Gradle configuration auto-installs the
      # Flutter-pinned NDK mid-build with no retry; one truncated
      # download reds the leg. Bounded-retry pre-install instead.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall

      # Same release keystore as the AAB job (contract: store and god sign
      # with the SAME release key — only the applicationId differs), same
      # strict-signing posture: no silent debug-signed APKs. No Play
      # service account here — god never touches Play.
      - name: Build flavor APK
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          # gh-1522: stamp the APK version strings from the derived tag
          # version — the committed pubspec is the static 0.0.0-dev
          # placeholder and never churns.
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}

runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64 git bootstrap (no official linux-arm64 Flutter tarball) — same
      # as the flutter-tests and pty-visual legs.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # gh-1538: the nightly cli-visual job is retired (this PR leg runs the
      # same suite pre-merge) — placeholder rationale lives with the
      # flutter-tests leg.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config that resolves package:flutter_agent_harness
      # to the pub-cache copy (an old published build) and the CLI dies on
      # compile errors before the first frame. flutter_app's pub get only
      # writes flutter_app/.dart_tool — the root needs its own.
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: flutter test cli_visual (settings hub flows only)
        run: >-
          cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual/fa_cli_visual_test.dart
          --tags integration --name "settings hub → (compaction|memory)"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-settings-screenshots
          path: test/integration/screenshots/
          retention-days: 7

  # Aggregate required check: branch protection requires ONE stable context.
  # Skipped legs (path-filtered out) count as pass — a docs PR must go green
  # on static alone.

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #280: PR-level BUILD verification. The gates above analyze and
  # test but never COMPILE a platform target — a PR could go green while
  # breaking the iOS/macOS/Android/web build (pod/entitlement drift,
  # web-only compile errors, asset manifest breakage), discovered later by
  # build-mobile.yml/build-macos.yml at release time. Four parallel debug
  # legs below close that gap, gated on app/shared changes only (docs/core
  # PRs never pay). Debug mode on PRs: compile-truth is the goal; release-
  # only concerns (tree-shaking, R8, codesign) live in the nightly release
  # matrix (nightly.yml). Budgets (#177): ≤8 min warm / ≤15 min cold per
  # leg, ≤10 min wall added to an app-touching PR (legs run in parallel).
  # E4: both macOS legs use GitHub-hosted macos-latest — every job gets its
  # own ephemeral VM, so ios+macos are never serialized on one runner (and
  # PR code never lands on the self-hosted release pool).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  build-web:
    name: Build web (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Pinned to the same SDK as the release path (#281): 3.47.x. The
      # action's cache key embeds the resolved SDK version, so an SDK bump
      # in a PR never restores a poisoned cache (E1).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: flutter build web
        # E3: warnings (including the Wasm dry-run diagnostics) are allowed;
        # compile errors fail via the exit code — same fatal semantics as
        # the flutter-tests leg's analyze step.
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build web

  build-android:
    name: Build Android APK (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The google-services Gradle plugin (applied unconditionally in
      # android/app/build.gradle.kts) refuses to run without this file.
      # #622 commits a placeholder carrying BOTH flavor clients
      # (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god); keep it whenever present — the
      # debug-APK smoke pins the store flavor (`--flavor store`, only the
      # dev.fa1.app client is needed); god compile truth is covered by the
      # flavor matrix release job. Only when the file is missing
      # (old forks/history) seed the structurally-valid dev.fa1.app
      # placeholder — debug APKs never talk to Firebase with it; the goal
      # here is compile truth (#280).
      - name: Create placeholder google-services.json
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f android/app/google-services.json ]; then
            echo "committed google-services.json present (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god) — keeping it"
          else
            cat > android/app/google-services.json << 'EOF'
          {
            "project_info": {
              "project_number": "000000000000",
              "project_id": "fa1-placeholder",
              "storage_bucket": "fa1-placeholder.appspot.com"
            },
            "client": [
              {
                "client_info": {
                  "mobilesdk_app_id": "1:000000000000:android:0000000000000000000000",
                  "android_client_info": {
                    "package_name": "dev.fa1.app"
                  }
                },
                "oauth_client": [],
                "api_key": [
                  {
                    "current_key": "AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000"
                  }
                ],
                "services": {
                  "appinvite_service": {
                    "other_platform_oauth_client": []
                  }
                }
              }
            ],
            "configuration_version": "1"
          }
          EOF
          fi

    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # bf81411e added GoogleService-Info.plist to the Runner target
      # resources (a hard build input). The real plist is gitignored; the
      # release path writes it from GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64
      # (build-mobile.yml), but PR legs have no such secret — seed a
      # placeholder, same trick as the android leg's placeholder
      # google-services.json. Xcode only copies the file; Firebase reads
      # it at app runtime, never at build time.
      - name: Write placeholder GoogleService-Info.plist (iOS)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > flutter_app/ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist << 'EOF'
          <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
          <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
          <plist version="1.0">
          <dict>
          	<key>GOOGLE_APP_ID</key>
          	<string>1:000000000000:ios:0000000000000000000000</string>
          	<key>API_KEY</key>
          	<string>AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000</string>
          	<key>PROJECT_ID</key>
          	<string>fa1-placeholder</string>
          	<key>PROJECT_NUMBER</key>
          	<string>000000000000</string>
          	<key>BUNDLE_ID</key>
          	<string>dev.fa1.app</string>
          	<key>GCM_SENDER_ID</key>
          	<string>000000000000</string>
          	<key>IS_ANALYTICS_ENABLED</key>
          	<false/>
          	<key>IS_CRASHLYTICS_ENABLED</key>
          	<false/>
          </dict>
          </plist>
          EOF
          plutil -lint flutter_app/ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist

      # E2: pods cache keyed on Podfile.lock AND a weekly-rolled epoch, so
      # CocoaPods spec drift is re-verified at least weekly even when the
      # lockfile is unchanged. restore-keys falls back to last week's
      # same-lock cache (never a cross-lock cache).
      - name: Compute weekly pods-cache epoch
        id: week
        run: echo "epoch=$(date -u +%Y-W%V)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Cache CocoaPods (iOS)
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: flutter_app/ios/Pods
          key: ios-pods-ci-v1-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/ios/Podfile.lock') }}-${{ steps.week.outputs.epoch }}
          restore-keys: |
            ios-pods-ci-v1-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/ios/Podfile.lock') }}-

      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git (the release path
          # prefers the self-hosted runner's local copy; GitHub-hosted PR
          # legs always take the pinned upstream fallback).
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks"
          rm -rf "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          # --retry alone skips transient mid-transfer resets (curl 56).
          curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
            -o /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip \
            https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip
          unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"

name: android-ndk-preinstall
description: >-
  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK and the AGP-default CMake so
  Gradle configuration never triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download
  mid-build. gh-1655: one truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download
  ("Error on ZipFile unknown archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android
  leg — and the aggregate Quality gate with it — because AGP's
  in-configuration auto-install path has NO retry. gh-1757: the same leg
  died the same way on the sibling component — the `:jni` module
  (transitive `jni` package via path_provider_android) wires
  externalNativeBuild.cmake with no version, so AGP auto-installs its
  default cmake;3.22.1 mid-configuration and one corrupt archive
  ("Archive is not a ZIP archive") red'd v1.0.619's build-android leg, the
  aggregate Quality gate, and the Advance vpinned marker job with it. The
  NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's own gradle plugin
  source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves to — no second pin
  to drift), the CMake version is the AGP default cross-checked against
  the AGP pin by the guard test, both installs are skipped when the
  component is already present, and each download is bounded-retried —
  the same hardening the (since-removed) flutter_gemma Android seed
  carried (gh-1468).
  Companion guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK + AGP-default CMake (bounded retry)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
        else
          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
            exit 1
          fi
          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
        fi
        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
        fi
        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
        # the NDK is fully installed. gh-1757: the same Gradle
        # configuration step also provisions CMake — the `:jni` module
        # (transitive `jni` package via path_provider_android) wires
        # externalNativeBuild.cmake with no version, so AGP falls back
        # to its default 3.22.1 (the AGP pin lives in
        # flutter_app/android/settings.gradle.kts; the guard test
        # cross-checks the coupling) and auto-installs it
        # mid-configuration with no retry when
        # $ANDROID_HOME/cmake/<version> is missing. Both lookups mirror
        # exactly what AGP performs: a provisioned component means the
        # pre-install is a no-op.
        NEEDS_NDK=1
        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
          NEEDS_NDK=0
        fi
        CMAKE_VERSION="3.22.1"
        NEEDS_CMAKE=1
        if [ -x "$ANDROID_SDK/cmake/$CMAKE_VERSION/bin/cmake" ]; then
          echo "CMake $CMAKE_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
          NEEDS_CMAKE=0
        fi
        if [ "$NEEDS_NDK" = "0" ] && [ "$NEEDS_CMAKE" = "0" ]; then
          echo "NDK and CMake already provisioned — nothing to pre-install"
          exit 0
        fi
        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
        # gh-1757 first: CMake is the smaller download and the failure
        # v1.0.619 actually hit (`:jni:configureCMakeDebug`).
        if [ "$NEEDS_CMAKE" = "1" ]; then
          CMAKE_OK=0
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            echo "installing CMake $CMAKE_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
            rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/cmake/$CMAKE_VERSION"
            if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "cmake;$CMAKE_VERSION" && [ -x "$ANDROID_SDK/cmake/$CMAKE_VERSION/bin/cmake" ]; then
              echo "CMake $CMAKE_VERSION installed"
              CMAKE_OK=1
              break
            fi
            echo "::warning::sdkmanager CMake install failed or bin/cmake missing (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$CMAKE_OK" = "0" ]; then
            echo "::error::CMake $CMAKE_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1757: the :jni module auto-installs it mid-build with no retry, and one corrupt archive (\"Archive is not a ZIP archive\") red'd v1.0.619's build-android leg; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
            exit 1
          fi
        fi
        if [ "$NEEDS_NDK" = "1" ]; then
          NDK_OK=0
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
            rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
            if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
              echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
              NDK_OK=1
              break
            fi
            echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$NDK_OK" = "0" ]; then
            echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
            exit 1
          fi
        fi

4. **A different, MUCH more elegant choke point: make the download itself retry — by overriding the sqlite3 package resolution? NO (see above).**

858:  test-core:
  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # gh-1778: 20 min — sized for the degraded-cache worst case, not just
    # the warm wall. Warm shards take ~460-525 s (run 39703080550) but the
    # v1.0.621 release run stalled ~133 s on EACH cache step (degraded
    # GitHub cache service, keys that existed) and needed ~14 min cold —
    # cancelled at the 12-min wall with 2535/2761 tests green, reding the
    # whole release. 20 clears that worst case and sits in the sibling
    # test-leg band (flutter-tests 20, integration-mock 25, pty 40); a
    # genuinely hung shard is still killed loudly.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      # gh-1778: caches are best-effort — a restore that hangs (degraded
      # cache service stalled both steps ~133 s on the v1.0.621 release
      # run) or fails only means slower setup. Step-level 2-min cap bounds
      # the stall; continue-on-error keeps a dead cache from reding the
      # shard (unlike the gh-1724 evidence uploads, which stay loud).
      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-
        timeout-minutes: 2
        continue-on-error: true

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
        timeout-minutes: 2
        continue-on-error: true

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced

name: 'Flutter pub get (enforced lockfile, bounded retry)'
description: >-
  The ONE sanctioned flutter_app dependency-resolution step:
  `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` with the #726 bounded retry. pub
  has no retry for its git-dependency mirror clones (flutter_js,
  flutter_js_widget_runtime) — one transient "Connection reset by peer" on
  github.com:443 failed the whole leg (#726 on the iOS release leg; gh-1310
  on ci.yml build-macos, where the v1.0.516 lockfile refresh cold-missed
  the flutter-action pub cache and forced fresh clones exactly when a
  release lands). Deterministic pubspec/lockfile skews (gh-1299: a release
  commit that bumps the version without regenerating flutter_app/
  pubspec.lock) fail identically on every attempt — the loop detects the
  "Unable to satisfy" signature and fails fast instead of burning ~30s per
  red leg and blaming the network (PR #1268 review thread 3). Guarded by
  test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart: no workflow run-step may resolve
  flutter_app itself.

inputs:
  working-directory:
    description: 'Directory holding the pubspec.yaml to resolve.'
    required: false
    default: flutter_app

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile (bounded retry, #726)
      working-directory: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
      env:
        # Git-dep clones must never hang a leg on a credential prompt.
        GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        LOG_FILE="$(mktemp)"
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
          if flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_FILE"; then
            rm -f "$LOG_FILE"
            exit 0
          fi
          # A pubspec/lockfile skew is deterministic — retrying cannot
          # fix it, so fail fast instead of burning ~30s per red leg and
          # blaming the network (PR #1268 review thread 3).
          if grep -qE 'Unable to satisfy .* using .*pubspec\.lock' "$LOG_FILE"; then
            echo "::error::$PWD/pubspec.lock is out of sync with $PWD/pubspec.yaml — regenerate it (cd $PWD && flutter pub get) and commit; not retrying a deterministic skew"
            rm -f "$LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
            echo "::error::flutter pub get failed after 3 attempts — the runner's network to pub.dev/github.com is unhealthy"
            rm -f "$LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "::warning::flutter pub get failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 15s"
          sleep 15
        done

"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out


def file_has_tag(path: str, tag: str) -> bool:
    """True when the file's real (non-comment) code names `tag` in @Tags([...])."""
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            head = f.read()
    except OSError:
        return False
    # Full read: a truncated scan would silently drop a tagged file from
    # the bin-pack safety net; @Tags lives anywhere in the file's metadata.
    # But match CODE only — strip the `//` portion of every line first. A
    # `///` doc comment that merely MENTIONS `@Tags(['io', 'integration'])`
    # once phantom-tagged test/cli/fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test.dart into
    # the integration manifest (review #963): the file has no integration
    # tag and the shard step runs zero tests from it.
    code = "\n".join(re.sub(r"//.*", "", line) for line in head.splitlines())
    return re.search(r"@Tags\s*\(\s*\[[^\]]*['\"]" + re.escape(tag) + r"['\"]", code) is not None


def uncovered_files(covered: set, root: str, exclude: list,
                    required_tag=None, exclude_tags=None) -> list:
    """Individual test files missing from a file-level manifest, as (path, 1).

    Default (no required_tag): files under test/ excluding integration and
    --exclude matches — the core/faui manifests. With required_tag (e.g.
    the integration shards, issue #931): only files whose @Tags annotation
    names the tag — an integration manifest must never bin-pack untagged
    core files (they would be filtered out by --tags anyway, but selecting
    them is noise) and must NOT skip test/integration. With exclude_tags
    (gh-1199 AC1): files carrying an excluded tag stay out even when they
    match required_tag — the live boundary holds for runtime bin-packs.
    """
    out = []
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)):
        norm = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if any(x in norm for x in exclude):
            continue
        if required_tag is None:
            if "/integration/" in norm:
                continue  # integration runs in its own CI job; excludes stay out
        elif not file_has_tag(path, required_tag):
            continue
        if exclude_tags and any(file_has_tag(path, t) for t in exclude_tags):
            continue
        if norm not in covered:
            out.append((norm, 1))
    return out


def bin_pack_by_count(units: list, n: int) -> list:
    buckets = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    loads = [0] * n
    for unit, count in sorted(units, key=lambda u: -u[1]):
        i = loads.index(min(loads))
        buckets[i].append(unit)
        loads[i] += count
    return buckets

# Root Cause Analysis ## Root Cause Analysis **Bug**: The v1.0.697 tag run (run 42567244226) red'd four CI jobs — `Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)`, `Flutter app tests (shard 0/2)`, `Flutter app tests (shard 1/2)`, `Build Android APK (debug)` — and the aggregate `Quality gate` with them, while the identical tree (sha 9550c02) had passed the full SM validation run hours earlier (run 42521681812, 2026-11-08 20:44, green). **Root cause**: All four jobs died inside the `sqlite3` package's native-assets build hook. `sqlite3` 3.7.0 (pinned by the committed `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, pulled in via `flutter_agent_memory`; the floating root lockfile resolves 3.9.1 with the same behavior) downloads its prebuilt `libsqlite3..` binary at BUILD time from `https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases/download/sqlite3-3.7.0/` (hook: `lib/src/hook/compile/description.dart`, `PrecompiledFromGithubAssets._fetchFromSource`). That hook performs a SINGLE attempt with NO HTTP status check: it pipes the response body straight into the output file and only verifies the sha256 afterwards. During the 05:25 run the runner egress intermittently answered `504 Gateway Time-out` for release-asset downloads; the hook saved the 92-byte HTML error page as the library file and its own hash check then threw: ``` Bad state: Hash of downloaded file libsqlite3.arm64.linux.so is bef140a1a96994029153dca8c00b1750b9a5a764fb9db2dc68d7bb40e8a29e8a, expected 037539c68603ce1dbff411c276945e092b808d48d515e5e15d5266a602d39711. ``` Evidence chain: - The failing hash `bef140a1…` is IDENTICAL for two different files (`libsqlite3.arm64.linux.so` on the three linux legs, `libsqlite3.arm.android.so` on the android leg) — one shared error page, not per-file corruption. `sha256sum` of the 92-byte `

504 Gateway Time-out

…` page is exactly `bef140a1…` (reproduced locally). - The upstream release `sqlite3-3.7.0` is intact; a live download returns sha256 `037539c6…`, matching the pinned hash. - Reproduced locally in this sandbox: `cd flutter_app && flutter test …` fails with the same `Bad state` while the egress 504s, and succeeds when the download gets through — pure network roulette, zero code faults. **Impact**: Every CI leg that compiles the root package (`dart test`/`dart run`/`dart build` — test-core shards, static, hostile-env, pty legs, guards, dep-audit, perf-gate, usage-fold, release-provenance, …) or `flutter_app` (`flutter test`/`flutter build` — flutter-tests, pty-visual, cli-visual-settings, exzone, android/iOS/macOS builds) rolls a single-attempt dice against `github.com` release assets. One flaky 504 reds the leg AND the aggregate Quality gate, which blocks the release train (publish, binaries, vpinned marker advance). At v1.0.697 the dice came up 504 on four legs; the same tree was green at 20:44. **Fix approach**: Move the flaky download OUT of the unretryable mid-build hook path — the exact cure gh-1655 (NDK) and gh-1757 (CMake) established for this failure class: - `scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm.dart`: resolves the installed `sqlite3` package from each package config, parses the pinned `asset_hashes.dart` (single source of truth — no second pin to drift), and downloads the requested prebuilt libraries with bounded retry, HTTP-status checking, sha256 verification, and atomic writes into the hook's own cache (`/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/download-/libsqlite3.so`). The hook's reuse path (`downloadedFile.existsSync()` + hash match) then never touches the network. - `.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm`: composite action wrapper (targets input: `auto` / `android` / `arm64-ios` / explicit), wired after pub get in every hook-building leg; also appended to the shared `flutter-pub-get` action so every flutter leg is covered by one edit. - Guard test `test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart` pins the action, the wiring map and the ordering (before the first build/test step), in the style of `test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart`; `test/scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm_test.dart` covers the script deterministically against a local HTTP fixture (504-then-200 retry proof, status-blind and hash-mismatch rejections, idempotent reuse, cache repair). **Previous attempt**: None — first dev leg for gh-2072 (the earlier 05:48 machine run died in 1 min before any analysis).

(The bash_tools.md warning about `$?` after pipes — exactly the pitfall.) The script itself presumably exited 1; the pipe consumed it. Fine.
- The fixture parse still fails — because my /tmp/dbg fixture hash is 62 chars (regex {64} correctly rejects). The script logic is right; the fixture is wrong. Fix the test vector + this debug fixture understanding.

Now — update the ACTION design: invoke the script via plain `dart scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm.dart ...` — no hook build. But careful: the script uses `Process.runSync('uname')` — fine.

ALSO — the script test uses `Platform.resolvedExecutable` + `['run', scriptPath, ...]` — must change to plain `[scriptPath, ...]` (no `run`) so the test subprocess doesn't build root hooks either (test speed + no network roulette in the gate!). Plain `dart <path>` from the repo root — the entry script is INSIDE the root package... does plain path execution avoid hooks even inside a package? Option A ran from the repo root with the script inside scripts/ — NO hooks ✓ (proven above).

Hmm wait — actually, is that stable across dart versions? `dart <path>` runs the file as a script; hooks are built by the package-config-aware runner (`dart run`)... In newer SDKs plain path execution ALSO builds assets? The evidence here (SDK 3.47-ish stable): no hooks. CI pins dart stable via setup-dart — floating... If a future SDK starts building hooks on plain path execution, the prewarm step itself rolls the dice again. Mitigation: run the script from a directory WITHOUT a package config? The script's own cwd doesn't matter for hook building — the ENTRY SCRIPT's package context matters (root's .dart_tool). Copying the script to $RUNER_TEMP and running `dart $RUNER_TEMP/prewarm.dart` from the action — entry outside any package → no package config → no hooks even on future SDKs. name: sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
description: >-
  Prewarm the sqlite3 package's native-assets hook cache with bounded
  retry. gh-2072: the hook downloads `libsqlite3.<abi>.<os>` from the
  simolus3/sqlite3.dart GitHub release at build time in a SINGLE attempt
  with NO HTTP status check — at v1.0.697 the runner egress answered a
  transient `504 Gateway Time-out` HTML page, the hook saved that page as
  the library file, its own sha256 check threw
  `Bad state: Hash of downloaded file … is bef140a1… expected …`, and
  four CI legs (Terminal visual, Flutter app tests shards 0/2 + 1/2,
  Build Android APK) plus the aggregate Quality gate went red on a tree
  that had passed the same legs hours earlier. The same head later built
  green: pure network roulette, and every `dart test`/`dart run`/`dart
  build` leg and every `flutter test`/`flutter build` leg rolls it once
  per run.
  The prewarm reads the pinned hashes from the INSTALLED sqlite3 package
  (asset_hashes.dart — single source of truth, no second pin to drift),
  downloads with bounded retry + status check + sha256 verification, and
  writes atomically into the hook's own reuse cache
  (<root>/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/download-<hash8>/),
  so the hook never touches the network. Idempotent: a matching cached
  file is a no-op. Companion guard:
  test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart; script contract tested by
  test/scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm_test.dart.
inputs:
  package-roots:
    description: >-
      Space-separated package directories whose dependency graph carries
      sqlite3 (each must have .dart_tool/package_config.json — run this
      AFTER pub get). Defaults to the working directory.
    required: false
    default: '.'
  targets:
    description: >-
      `auto` (the host platform — the default), `android` (the three APK
      ABIs: arm, arm64, x64), `arm64-ios`, or explicit `<abi>-<os>` names
      (comma/space separated, e.g. `arm64-linux, x64-linux`). Targets
      whose pinned hash the installed sqlite3 package does not ship fail
      the step EXCEPT the auto host target, which skips cleanly (some
      hosts — windows, web — build no code assets at all).
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  attempts:
    description: 'Bounded-retry budget per file (default 4, backoff 5s/10s/20s).'
    required: false
    default: '4'
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Prewarm sqlite3 native-assets (bounded retry, gh-2072)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        DART_BIN="$(command -v dart || true)"
        if [ -z "$DART_BIN" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot locate dart on PATH — the sqlite3 native-assets prewarm needs the Dart SDK (wire it after pub get, before the first build/test step)"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Copy the script OUT of the workspace before invoking it: plain
        # `dart <path>` inside a package whose graph carries sqlite3
        # would build that package's OWN native-assets hooks first — the
        # exact single-attempt download this action exists to bypass —
        # and die on the very 504 it is defending against. A script
        # outside any package resolves no package config, builds no
        # hooks, and only reads the target packages' configs as data.
        SCRIPT_COPY="$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm.dart"
        cp scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm.dart "$SCRIPT_COPY"
        ARGS=()
        for root in ${{ inputs.package-roots }}; do
          ARGS+=(--package-root "$root")
        done
        ARGS+=(--targets "${{ inputs.targets }}")
        ARGS+=(--attempts "${{ inputs.attempts }}")
        if "$DART_BIN" "$SCRIPT_COPY" "${ARGS[@]}"; then
          exit 0
        fi
        echo "::error::sqlite3 native-assets prewarm failed after ${{ inputs.attempts }} attempts per target — gh-2072: the sqlite3 hook downloads prebuilt binaries mid-build with no status check and no retry; one transient GitHub error page reds the leg and the aggregate Quality gate. Inspect the attempts above; the guard (test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart) pins this wiring."
        exit 1

    # gh-2072: prewarm the sqlite3 package's native-assets hook cache — the
    # hook downloads `libsqlite3.<abi>.<os>` from GitHub releases at build

    # `504 Gateway Time-out` error page red'd four legs and the aggregate
    # Quality gate at v1.0.697 (a tree that had passed the same legs hours
    # earlier). Every flutter leg resolves flutter_app THROUGH THIS ACTION,
    # so the prewarm here covers the whole flutter class with one edit;
    # root-package (`dart test`) legs carry the explicit invocation pinned
    # by test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart. Host-auto targets: iOS
    # and Android APK/AAB legs add an explicit cross-target invocation
    # beside their NDK pre-install. Idempotent + a clean no-op when the
    # package graph carries no sqlite3.
    - name: Prewarm sqlite3 native-assets (bounded retry, gh-2072)
      working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
      shell: bash
      env:
        PREWARM_PACKAGE_ROOTS: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        DART_BIN="$(command -v dart || true)"
        if [ -z "$DART_BIN" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot locate dart on PATH — the sqlite3 native-assets prewarm needs the Dart SDK"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Copy the script OUT of the workspace before invoking it: plain
        # `dart <path>` inside a package whose graph carries sqlite3
        # would build that package's OWN native-assets hooks first — the
        # exact single-attempt download this step exists to bypass. A
        # script outside any package resolves no package config and
        # builds no hooks; it only reads the target packages' configs as
        # data.
        SCRIPT_COPY="$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm.dart"
        cp scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm.dart "$SCRIPT_COPY"
        ARGS=()
        for root in $PREWARM_PACKAGE_ROOTS; do
          ARGS+=(--package-root "$root")
        done
        # auto = the host platform: covers `flutter test` legs and the
        # desktop build targets (macos/linux/windows rows build no web or
        # cross targets here). Android/iOS device targets are provisioned
        # by the explicit cross-target invocations in the build legs.
        ARGS+=(--targets auto)
        ARGS+=(--attempts 4)
        if ! "$DART_BIN" "$SCRIPT_COPY" "${ARGS[@]}"; then
          echo "::error::sqlite3 native-assets prewarm failed — gh-2072: the sqlite3 hook downloads prebuilt binaries mid-build with no status check and no retry; one transient GitHub error page reds the leg and the aggregate Quality gate. Inspect the attempts above; the wiring guard is test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart."

release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa, build-extension]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
