# Root Cause Analysis ## Root Cause Analysis **Bug**: The v1.0.697 tag run (run 42567244226) red'd four CI jobs — `Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)`, `Flutter app tests (shard 0/2)`, `Flutter app tests (shard 1/2)`, `Build Android APK (debug)` — and the aggregate `Quality gate` with them, while the identical tree (sha 9550c02) had passed the full SM validation run hours earlier (run 42521681812, 2026-11-08 20:44, green). **Root cause**: All four jobs died inside the `sqlite3` package's native-assets build hook. `sqlite3` 3.7.0 (pinned by the committed `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, pulled in via `flutter_agent_memory`; the floating root lockfile resolves 3.9.1 with the same behavior) downloads its prebuilt `libsqlite3..` binary at BUILD time from `https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases/download/sqlite3-3.7.0/` (hook: `lib/src/hook/compile/description.dart`, `PrecompiledFromGithubAssets._fetchFromSource`). That hook performs a SINGLE attempt with NO HTTP status check: it pipes the response body straight into the output file and only verifies the sha256 afterwards. During the 05:25 run the runner egress intermittently answered `504 Gateway Time-out` for release-asset downloads; the hook saved the 92-byte HTML error page as the library file and its own hash check then threw: ``` Bad state: Hash of downloaded file libsqlite3.arm64.linux.so is bef140a1a96994029153dca8c00b1750b9a5a764fb9db2dc68d7bb40e8a29e8a, expected 037539c68603ce1dbff411c276945e092b808d48d515e5e15d5266a602d39711. ``` Evidence chain: - The failing hash `bef140a1…` is IDENTICAL for two different files (`libsqlite3.arm64.linux.so` on the three linux legs, `libsqlite3.arm.android.so` on the android leg) — one shared error page, not per-file corruption. `sha256sum` of the 92-byte `

504 Gateway Time-out

…` page is exactly `bef140a1…` (reproduced locally). - The upstream release `sqlite3-3.7.0` is intact; a live download returns sha256 `037539c6…`, matching the pinned hash. - Reproduced locally in this sandbox: `cd flutter_app && flutter test …` fails with the same `Bad state` while the egress 504s, and succeeds when the download gets through — pure network roulette, zero code faults. **Impact**: Every CI leg that compiles the root package (`dart test`/`dart run`/`dart build` — test-core shards, static, hostile-env, pty legs, guards, dep-audit, perf-gate, usage-fold, release-provenance, …) or `flutter_app` (`flutter test`/`flutter build` — flutter-tests, pty-visual, cli-visual-settings, exzone, android/iOS/macOS builds) rolls a single-attempt dice against `github.com` release assets. One flaky 504 reds the leg AND the aggregate Quality gate, which blocks the release train (publish, binaries, vpinned marker advance). At v1.0.697 the dice came up 504 on four legs; the same tree was green at 20:44. **Fix approach**: Move the flaky download OUT of the unretryable mid-build hook path — the exact cure gh-1655 (NDK) and gh-1757 (CMake) established for this failure class: - `scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm.dart`: resolves the installed `sqlite3` package from each package config, parses the pinned `asset_hashes.dart` (single source of truth — no second pin to drift), and downloads the requested prebuilt libraries with bounded retry, HTTP-status checking, sha256 verification, and atomic writes into the hook's own cache (`/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/download-/libsqlite3.so`). The hook's reuse path (`downloadedFile.existsSync()` + hash match) then never touches the network. - `.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm`: composite action wrapper (targets input: `auto` / `android` / `arm64-ios` / explicit), wired after pub get in every hook-building leg; also appended to the shared `flutter-pub-get` action so every flutter leg is covered by one edit. - Guard test `test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart` pins the action, the wiring map and the ordering (before the first build/test step), in the style of `test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart`; `test/scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm_test.dart` covers the script deterministically against a local HTTP fixture (504-then-200 retry proof, status-blind and hash-mismatch rejections, idempotent reuse, cache repair). **Previous attempt**: None — first dev leg for gh-2072 (the earlier 05:48 machine run died in 1 min before any analysis).

content.text:
name: 'Flutter pub get (enforced lockfile, bounded retry)'
description: >-
  The ONE sanctioned flutter_app dependency-resolution step:
  `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` with the #726 bounded retry. pub
  has no retry for its git-dependency mirror clones (flutter_js,
  flutter_js_widget_runtime) — one transient "Connection reset by peer" on
  github.com:443 failed the whole leg (#726 on the iOS release leg; gh-1310
  on ci.yml build-macos, where the v1.0.516 lockfile refresh cold-missed
  the flutter-action pub cache and forced fresh clones exactly when a
  release lands). Deterministic pubspec/lockfile skews (gh-1299: a release
  commit that bumps the version without regenerating flutter_app/
  pubspec.lock) fail identically on every attempt — the loop detects the
  "Unable to satisfy" signature and fails fast instead of burning ~30s per
  red leg and blaming the network (PR #1268 review thread 3). Guarded by
  test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart: no workflow run-step may resolve
  flutter_app itself.

inputs:
  working-directory:
    description: 'Directory holding the pubspec.yaml to resolve.'
    required: false
    default: flutter_app

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile (bounded retry, #726)
      working-directory: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
      env:
        # Git-dep clones must never hang a leg on a credential prompt.
        GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        LOG_FILE="$(mktemp)"
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
          if flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_FILE"; then
            rm -f "$LOG_FILE"
            exit 0
          fi
          # A pubspec/lockfile skew is deterministic — retrying cannot
          # fix it, so fail fast instead of burning ~30s per red leg and
          # blaming the network (PR #1268 review thread 3).
          if grep -qE 'Unable to satisfy .* using .*pubspec\.lock' "$LOG_FILE"; then
            echo "::error::$PWD/pubspec.lock is out of sync with $PWD/pubspec.yaml — regenerate it (cd $PWD && flutter pub get) and commit; not retrying a deterministic skew"
            rm -f "$LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
            echo "::error::flutter pub get failed after 3 attempts — the runner's network to pub.dev/github.com is unhealthy"
            rm -f "$LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "::warning::flutter pub get failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 15s"
          sleep 15
        done

    # gh-2072: prewarm the sqlite3 package's native-assets hook cache — the
    # hook downloads `libsqlite3.<abi>.<os>` from GitHub releases at build
    # time in a single attempt with no status check, and one transient
    # `504 Gateway Time-out` error page red'd four legs and the aggregate
    # Quality gate at v1.0.697 (a tree that had passed the same legs hours
    # earlier). Every flutter leg resolves flutter_app THROUGH THIS ACTION,
    # so the prewarm here covers the whole flutter class with one edit;
    # root-package (`dart test`) legs carry the explicit invocation pinned
    # by test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart. Host-auto targets: iOS
    # and Android APK/AAB legs add an explicit cross-target invocation
    # beside their NDK pre-install. Idempotent + a clean no-op when the
    # package graph carries no sqlite3.
    - name: Prewarm sqlite3 native-assets (bounded retry, gh-2072)
      working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
      shell: bash
      env:
        PREWARM_PACKAGE_ROOTS: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        DART_BIN="$(command -v dart || true)"
        if [ -z "$DART_BIN" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot locate dart on PATH — the sqlite3 native-assets prewarm needs the Dart SDK"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Copy the script OUT of the workspace before invoking it: plain
        # `dart <path>` inside a package whose graph carries sqlite3
        # would build that package's OWN native-assets hooks first — the
        # exact single-attempt download this step exists to bypass. A
        # script outside any package resolves no package config and
        # builds no hooks; it only reads the target packages' configs as
        # data.
        SCRIPT_COPY="$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm.dart"
        cp scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm.dart "$SCRIPT_COPY"
        ARGS=()
        for root in $PREWARM_PACKAGE_ROOTS; do
          ARGS+=(--package-root "$root")
        done
        # auto = the host platform: covers `flutter test` legs and the
        # desktop build targets (macos/linux/windows rows build no web or
        # cross targets here). Android/iOS device targets are provisioned
        # by the explicit cross-target invocations in the build legs.
        ARGS+=(--targets auto)
        ARGS+=(--attempts 4)
        if ! "$DART_BIN" "$SCRIPT_COPY" "${ARGS[@]}"; then
          echo "::error::sqlite3 native-assets prewarm failed — gh-2072: the sqlite3 hook downloads prebuilt binaries mid-build with no status check and no retry; one transient GitHub error page reds the leg and the aggregate Quality gate. Inspect the attempts above; the wiring guard is test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart."
          exit 1
        fi

Draft:
``
### Root Cause
The sqlite3 package's native-assets build hook downloads its prebuilt `libsqlite3.<abi>.<os>` binary at build time with a SINGLE attempt and no HTTP status check (`sqlite3 3.7.0`, `hook/compile/description.dart`). One transient GitHub `504 Gateway Time-out` was saved as the library file, the hook's own sha256 check threw, and four legs + the aggregate Quality gate red'd at v1.0.697 on a tree that had passed the same legs hours earlier.

### Fix
- `scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm.dart`: resolves the installed sqlite3 from each package config, parses the pinned `asset_hashes.dart` (no second pin), downloads the prebuilt libraries with bounded retry, status checks, sha256 verification and atomic writes straight into the hook's reuse cache (`<root>/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/download-<hash8>/`) — the hook then never touches the network.
- `.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm`: composite action (targets: `auto`/`android`/`arm64-ios`/explicit); wired before the first build/test step in every hook-building leg and appended to the shared `flutter-pub-get` action so every flutter leg is covered.
- `ci.yml` build-android/build-ios, `build-mobile.yml` and the `nightly.yml` release matrix request explicit cross-target binaries (APK ABIs / arm64-ios); windows/web rows skip (no code-asset hook).

### Test Coverage
- `test/scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm_test.dart` — 53 tests incl. 504-then-200 retry, status-blind + hash-mismatch rejection, corrupt-cache repair, clean no-op without sqlite3: PASED
- `test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart` — pins the wiring map/ordering/targets for all affected workflows: PASED
- Full ci-guard family: 264 tests passed; `ci_fast_gate.sh --hook`: <gate result>
- End-to-end proof: prewarm → hook reused the cached file (frozen mtime untouched, zero network).

### Notes
- `office_addin/dart` needed a local `dart pub get` for the fast gate analyze stage (sandbox-only; 47 identical errors on the base commit without it).
- The `sqlite3` 3.7.0 upstream release assets are intact (live download matches the pinned hash) — no upstream action needed.
``

content.text:
ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      - name: Install Flutter dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # gh-2072: prewarm the sqlite3 native-assets hook cache per matrix
      # row (bounded-retry download of the prebuilt binaries the hook
      # would otherwise fetch mid-build, unchecked, unretried — one
      # transient 504 error page red'd four legs at v1.0.697). android
      # rows need the APK ABI triple, ios rows the device binary, desktop
      # rows the host target (`auto`); web builds no code assets and
      # windows ships no libsqlite3 prebuilt at all (flutter builds no
      # code assets on that host — the hook no-ops), so those two rows
      # skip the prewarm entirely.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
        if: matrix.target == 'android' || matrix.target == 'ios' || matrix.target == 'macos' || matrix.target == 'linux'
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.sqlite3_targets }}

      # gh-1296 NG1/NG3: the scheduled legs are the drift detector — the
      # pod-sync half of the lockfile gate runs nightly (upstream spec drift
      # or a native plugin landing without / behind its pod lock reds the
      # scheduled build and the auto-issue leg files nightly-red) instead of
      # being first discovered by a random PR. The inventory half
      # (missing/untracked/gitignored lockfiles) is enforced in ci.yml
      # Static gates, not here.

But ALSO: does the flutter-pub-get action's built-in prewarm step run on windows with `--targets auto`? YES — every flutter leg via flutter-pub-get runs the prewarm with auto. On the windows runner, `auto` → 'x64-windows' → after my fix, asset `sqlite3.x64.windows.dll` → cached name `sqlite3.dll`. So the pub-get action ALONE covers windows rows! The matrix-level explicit step for windows is now redundant... but harmless (idempotent — script reuses). Actually WAIT — the pub-get action prewarm runs `--package-root ${{ inputs.working-directory }}` (flutter_app) and `--targets auto` — on windows it prewarms x64-windows ALREADY. My matrix step duplicates it. Hmm — the matrix step exists for CROSS targets (android ABIs, ios). For windows the host-auto already covers it. But leaving the explicit step with `targets: auto` is a harmless no-op duplication... but it's UGLY and could confuse reviewers. Also nightly macos/linux rows: pub-get action's auto prewarm ALSO covers them already! So the matrix step is only strictly needed for android/ios rows.

Decision: simplify — keep the matrix step for android/ios only (the cross targets), since desktop rows are covered by the action's auto prewarm. That reduces duplication AND matches the ci.yml build-macos precedent (intentionally absent from the map because flutter-pub-get's central prewarm covers it).

arguments.content:
### Root Cause
The `sqlite3` package's native-assets build hook downloads its prebuilt `libsqlite3.<abi>.<os>` binary at **build** time with a single attempt and no HTTP status check (`sqlite3` 3.7.0, `hook/compile/description.dart`, pinned by `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` via `flutter_agent_memory`). During the v1.0.697 run the runner egress answered `504 Gateway Time-out` for release-asset downloads; the hook saved the 92-byte HTML error page as the library and its own sha256 check threw (`Bad state: Hash of downloaded file … bef140a1a96994029153dca8c00b1750b9a5a764fb9db2dc68d7bb40e8a29e8a` — the exact hash of the 504 page, identical across four legs). Four CI legs + the aggregate Quality gate red'd on a tree that had passed the same legs hours earlier.

### Fix
- `scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm.dart`: resolves the installed `sqlite3` package from each package config, parses its pinned `asset_hashes.dart` (single source of truth — windows assets have no `lib` prefix: `sqlite3.x64.windows.dll`), downloads the requested prebuilt libraries with bounded retry, HTTP-status checks, sha256 verification and atomic writes into the hook's own reuse cache (`<root>/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/download-<hash8>/`), so the hook never touches the network.
- `.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm`: composite action (`targets`: `auto` / `android` / `arm64-ios` / explicit), wired before the first build/test step in every hook-building leg, and appended to the shared `flutter-pub-get` action so every flutter leg is covered by one edit.
- Explicit cross-target invocations: `ci.yml` build-android (APK ABIs) + build-ios (`arm64-ios`), `build-mobile.yml` (4 legs), the `nightly.yml` release matrix (`sqlite3_targets` per row; desktop rows covered by the central `auto` prewarm, web builds no code assets).
- `test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart` pins the wiring map, ordering (prewarm before any hook-building step) and explicit targets, in the style of the gh-1655 NDK guard.

### Test Coverage
- `test/scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm_test.dart` — 54 tests: 504-then-200 retry proof, status-blind and hash-mismatch rejection, corrupt-cache repair, clean no-op without sqlite3, unknown-target failure, windows/apple asset-naming pins — **PASSED**
- `test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart` + full ci-guard family — 264 tests — **PASSED**
- `bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook` — GATE_RESULT_PLACEHOLDER
- End-to-end proof on the real toolchain: prewarm → hook reused the cached file (frozen mtime untouched, zero network); control run without cache re-downloaded at the same path.

### Notes
- Upstream `sqlite3-3.7.0` release assets are intact (live download matches the pinned hash) — no upstream action needed.
- `office_addin/dart` needed a local `dart pub get` for the fast gate's analyze stage in this sandbox (447 identical analyzer errors on the base commit without it — pre-existing, unrelated).
- No new external dependencies: the prewarm downloads from the same `simolus3/sqlite3.dart` release the hook already targets.

# Root Cause Analysis ## Root Cause Analysis **Bug**: The v1.0.697 tag run (run 42567244226) red'd four CI jobs — `Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)`, `Flutter app tests (shard 0/2)`, `Flutter app tests (shard 1/2)`, `Build Android APK (debug)` — and the aggregate `Quality gate` with them, while the identical tree (sha 9550c02) had passed the full SM validation run hours earlier (run 42521681812, 2026-11-08 20:44, green). **Root cause**: All four jobs died inside the `sqlite3` package's native-assets build hook. `sqlite3` 3.7.0 (pinned by the committed `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, pulled in via `flutter_agent_memory`; the floating root lockfile resolves 3.9.1 with the same behavior) downloads its prebuilt `libsqlite3..` binary at BUILD time from `https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases/download/sqlite3-3.7.0/` (hook: `lib/src/hook/compile/description.dart`, `PrecompiledFromGithubAssets._fetchFromSource`). That hook performs a SINGLE attempt with NO HTTP status check: it pipes the response body straight into the output file and only verifies the sha256 afterwards. During the 05:25 run the runner egress intermittently answered `504 Gateway Time-out` for release-asset downloads; the hook saved the 92-byte HTML error page as the library file and its own hash check then threw: ``` Bad state: Hash of downloaded file libsqlite3.arm64.linux.so is bef140a1a96994029153dca8c00b1750b9a5a764fb9db2dc68d7bb40e8a29e8a, expected 037539c68603ce1dbff411c276945e092b808d48d515e5e15d5266a602d39711. ``` Evidence chain: - The failing hash `bef140a1…` is IDENTICAL for two different files (`libsqlite3.arm64.linux.so` on the three linux legs, `libsqlite3.arm.android.so` on the android leg) — one shared error page, not per-file corruption. `sha256sum` of the 92-byte `

504 Gateway Time-out

…` page is exactly `bef140a1…` (reproduced locally).
